production.note: US model years. First: for 2017 'the Scion FR-S adopts the Toyota 86 identity used in other global markets, as Scion and its models transition back to the Toyota brand'; the 2013 to 2016 car is the separate Scion FR-S record. Last: Toyota's newsroom has a 2020 Toyota 86 vehicle page with the release '2020 Toyota 86 Brings a Slice of Legendary Japanese Road to America' (21 October 2019) (toyota-us-2020-86-page); no 2021 Toyota 86 page exists (pressroom.toyota.com/vehicle/2021-toyota-86/ returns 404), and the successor is the 2022 GR86 (toyota-us-2022-gr86-thrills). No opened Toyota page says in so many words that 2020 was the last model year.

body.note: '2+2 sports car'; sold only as a coupe.

displacementL.note: 1,998 cc. The 2017 release gives litres only ('2.0-liter aluminum boxer engine'); Toyota's GR 86 release gives the old engine's cc: 'bumping up from 1,998cc to 2,387cc' (toyota-us-2022-gr86-thrills).

aspiration.note: Inferred: Toyota describes a 2.0-liter boxer four and mentions no turbocharger or supercharger.

fuel.note: Inferred from Toyota's description of a conventional piston engine.

drivetrain.note: 'the return of the fundamental, affordable rear-drive sports car'

powerHp.note: 2017 model year, manual. Quotes: "The 2.0-liter aluminum boxer engine delivers 205 hp at 7,000 rpm and 156 lb.-ft. of peak torque at 6,400 rpm." and "the 2.0-liter boxer four in the 2017 Toyota 86 M/T produces 205 hp and 156 lb.-ft. of torque while the automatic has 200 hp and 151 lb.-ft. of torque." The 2020 vehicle page still says 'With 205 horsepower moving about 2,800 pounds' (toyota-us-2020-86-page).

weightLb.note: 2017 model year, 6-speed manual. Quote: "At a svelte 2,758 lbs. (with six-speed manual transmission), the Toyota 86 is among the lightest sports cars on the market." The release names no trim; it is taken to be the standard car. Toyota's release does not use the word 'curb'; the figure matches the Scion FR-S brochure's labelled curb weight (2,758 lb manual) for the same car.
